props.name: hdr
props.doc:
Neon only: on a display that reports HDR, draw the light in a WebGPU
canvas with extended tone mapping, so the tubes run brighter than SDR
white and the beam peaks around 1000 nits. Elsewhere the CSS glow
stays on its own.

props.doc:
Plays a cue each time a mouse or pen plucks a line: `hover` for an
item's line, a softer `tick` for a ruler tick. Off by default; only
audible once the user has enabled sound.

props.name: variant
props.doc:
`"neon"` turns the lines into glowing tubes: proximity raises the glow,
a hot beam of light rides every pluck, labels glow on hover, and the
current line breathes. Made for dark surfaces.

The name of data.
This option will be used in tooltip and legend to represent a bar.
If no value was set to this option, the value of dataKey will be used alternatively.

props.name: formatter
props.doc:
Formats the value displayed in the tooltip for this Bar.
When set, takes precedence over the `formatter` prop on the Tooltip component.

props.name: legendType
props.doc: The type of icon in legend. If set to 'none', no legend item will be rendered.

props.name: minPointSize
props.doc:
The minimal height of a bar in a horizontal chart, or the minimal width of a bar in a vertical chart.

By default, 0 values are not shown.
To visualize a 0 (or close to zero) point, set the minimal point size to a pixel value like 3.

In stacked bar charts, minPointSize might not be respected for ti

props.name: maxBarSize
props.doc: The maximum width of bar in a horizontal chart, or maximum height in a vertical chart.

props.name: hide
props.doc:
Hides the whole graphical element when true.

Hiding an element is different from removing it from the chart:
Hidden graphical elements are still visible in Legend,
and can be included in axis domain calculations,
depending on `includeHidden` props of your XAxis/YAxis.

props.name: shape
props.doc:
If set a ReactElement, the shape of bar can be customized.
If set a function, the function will be called to render customized shape.
During animations, the function shape also receives `animationElapsedTime`, `isAnimating`, and `isEntrance`.
By default, renders a rectangle.

props.name: activeBar
background
radius
props.doc:
The radius of corners.

If you provide a single number, it applies to all four corners.
If you provide an array of four numbers, they apply to top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left corners respectively.

If set false, animation of bar will be disabled.
If set "auto", the animation will be disabled in SSR and will respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion system preference for accessibility.

props.name: animationDuration

props.name: animationEasing

props.name: animationInterpolateFn

Custom animation function for interpolating data items.
When provided, this replaces the default animation interpolation.

props.name: animationMatchBy
props.doc:
Strategy for matching previous items to next items during animation.
Determines how Recharts pairs old data points with new data points
to create smooth transitions.

- `matchAppend` (default): match sequentially by index and treat newly appended items as new
- `matchByIndex`: match by array positio

props.name: id
props.doc:
The unique identifier of this component.
Used as an HTML attribute `id`, and also to identify this element internally.

If undefined, Recharts will generate a unique ID automatically.

props.name: label
zIndex
props.doc:
Z-Index of this component and its children. The higher the value,
the more on top it will be rendered.
Components with higher zIndex will appear in front of components with lower zIndex.
If undefined or 0, the content is rendered in the default layer without portals.

props.name: dataKey
props.doc:
The data that you provide via the `data` prop is an array of objects.
Each object can have multiple properties, each representing a different data dimension.
Use the `dataKey` prop to specify which property (or dimension) to use for this component.

`domainMin`|`domainMax`. This looks like a small detail,

props.doc: The layout of chart defines the orientation of axes, graphical items, and tooltip.

props.name: maxBarSize
props.doc: The maximum width of all the bars in a horizontal BarChart, or maximum height in a vertical BarChart.

props.name: reverseStackOrder
props.doc:
If `false`, stacked items will be rendered left to right.
If `true`, stacked items will be rendered right to left.

Render direction affects SVG layering, not x position.

props.name: role
props.doc: The ARIA role for the chart, which provides semantic information for screen reader users.

props.name: stackOffset
props.doc:
The type of offset function used to generate the lower and upper values in the series array.
The types are built-in offsets in d3-shape.
Only applicable for stacked Area or Bar charts.
Has no effect when the stackId prop is not set on Area or Bar components.

Useful for setting the mouse cursor when hovering over the chart (e.g. `"pointer"`, `"crosshair"`).

Customize how the charts will synchronize tooltips and brushes.
`index`: synchronize using the data index in the data array. Index expects that all data has the same length.
`value`: synchronize using the data value on categorical axis (categorical: XAxis in horizontal layout, YAxis in vertical layo

If false, then it renders the chart at the specified width and height and will stay that way
even if the container size changes.

This is similar to ResponsiveContainer but without the need for an extra wrapp

Decides the time interval to throttle events.
Only events defined in `throttledEvents` prop are throttled.
All other events are executed immediately/synchronously.

Options:
- `number`: the time interval in milliseconds
- `'raf'`: use requestAnimationFrame to schedule updates.

props.name: throttledEvents
props.doc:
Defines which events should be throttled.
Events not in this list will not be throttled.

Use the special value `'all'` to throttle all events. Empty array means no events are throttled.

Use the prop `throttleDelay` to define the throttling interval.

If an event is on this list, then you lose the

props.doc: This event handler is called when a user right-clicks on an edge.

props.doc: This event handler is called when mouse of a user enters an edge.

props.doc: This event handler is called when mouse of a user moves over an edge.

props.name: onEdgeMouseLeave

props.name: onEdgeDoubleClick
props.doc: This event handler is called when a user double-clicks on an edge.

props.name: onReconnect
props.doc:
This handler is called when the source or target of a reconnectable edge is dragged from the
current node. It will fire even if the edge's source or target do not end up changing.
You can use the `reconnectEdge` utility to convert the connection to a new edge.

props.name: onReconnectStart
props.type: (event: MouseEvent<Element, MouseEvent>, edge: EdgeType, handleType: HandleType) => void
props.doc: This event fires when the user begins dragging the source or target of an editable edge.

props.name: onReconnectEnd
props.type: (event: MouseEvent | TouchEvent, edge: EdgeType, handleType: HandleType, connectionState: FinalConnectionState) => void
props.doc:
This event fires when the user releases the source or target of an editable edge. It is called
even if an edge update does not occur.

props.name: onNodesChange
props.doc:
Use this event handler to add interactivity to a controlled flow.
It is called on node drag, select, and move.

props.name: onEdgesChange
props.doc:
Use this event handler to add interactivity to a controlled flow. It is called on edge select
and remove.

props.name: onNodesDelete
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a node is deleted.

props.name: onEdgesDelete
props.doc: This event handler gets called when an edge is deleted.

props.name: onDelete
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a node or edge is deleted.

props.name: onSelectionDragStart
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a user starts to drag a selection box.

props.name: onSelectionDrag
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a user drags a selection box.

props.name: onSelectionDragStop
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a user stops dragging a selection box.

props.name: onSelectionContextMenu
props.doc: This event handler is called when a user right-clicks on a node selection.

props.name: onConnect
props.doc:
When a connection line is completed and two nodes are connected by the user, this event fires with the new connection.
You can use the `addEdge` utility to convert the connection to a complete edge.

props.name: onConnectStart
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a user starts to drag a connection line.

props.name: onConnectEnd
props.doc:
This callback will fire regardless of whether a valid connection could be made or not. You can
use the second `connectionState` parameter to have different behavior when a connection was
unsuccessful.

props.name: onInit
props.doc:
The `onInit` callback is called when the viewport is initialized. At this point you can use the
instance to call methods like `fitView` or `zoomTo`.

props.name: onMove
props.doc: This event handler is called while the user is either panning or zooming the viewport.

props.name: onMoveStart
props.doc: This event handler is called when the user begins to pan or zoom the viewport.

props.name: onMoveEnd
props.doc:
This event handler is called when panning or zooming viewport movement stops.
If the movement is not user-initiated, the event parameter will be `null`.

props.name: onSelectionChange
props.doc: This event handler gets called when a user changes group of selected elements in the flow.

props.name: onPaneScroll
props.doc: This event handler gets called when user scroll inside the pane.

props.name: onPaneClick
props.doc: This event handler gets called when user clicks inside the pane.

props.name: onPaneContextMenu
props.doc: This event handler gets called when user right clicks inside the pane.

props.name: onPaneMouseEnter
props.doc: This event handler gets called when mouse enters the pane.

props.name: onPaneMouseMove
props.doc: This event handler gets called when mouse moves over the pane.

props.name: onPaneMouseLeave
props.doc: This event handler gets called when mouse leaves the pane.

props.name: paneClickDistance
props.doc: Distance that the mouse can move between mousedown/up that will trigger a click.

props.name: nodeClickDistance
props.doc: Distance that the mouse can move between mousedown/up that will trigger a click.

props.name: onBeforeDelete
props.doc:
This handler is called before nodes or edges are deleted, allowing the deletion to be aborted
by returning `false` or modified by returning updated nodes and edges.

props.name: nodeTypes
props.doc:
Custom node types to be available in a flow.
React Flow matches a node's type to a component in the `nodeTypes` object.

props.name: edgeTypes
props.doc:
Custom edge types to be available in a flow.
React Flow matches an edge's type to a component in the `edgeTypes` object.
props.default:
{
default: BezierEdge,
straight: StraightEdge,
step: StepEdge,
smoothstep: SmoothStepEdge,
simplebezier: SimpleBezier
}

props.name: connectionLineType
props.doc:
The type of edge path to use for connection lines.
Although created edges can be of any type, React Flow needs to know what type of path to render for the connection line before the edge is created!

props.name: connectionLineStyle
props.doc: Styles to be applied to the connection line.

props.name: connectionLineComponent
props.doc: React Component to be used as a connection line.

props.name: connectionLineContainerStyle
props.doc: Styles to be applied to the container of the connection line.

props.name: connectionMode
props.doc:
A loose connection mode will allow you to connect handles with differing types, including
source-to-source connections. However, it does not support target-to-target connections. Strict
mode allows only connections between source handles and target handles.

props.name: deleteKeyCode
props.doc:
If set, pressing the key or chord will delete any selected nodes and edges. Passing an array
represents multiple keys that can be pressed.

For example, `["Delete", "Backspace"]` will delete selected elements when either key is pressed.

props.name: selectionKeyCode
props.doc:
If set, holding this key will let you click and drag to draw a selection box around multiple
nodes and edges. Passing an array represents multiple keys that can be pressed.

For example, `["Shift", "Meta"]` will allow you to draw a selection box when either key is
pressed.

props.name: selectionOnDrag
props.doc: Select multiple elements with a selection box, without pressing down `selectionKey`.

props.name: selectionMode
props.doc:
When set to `"partial"`, when the user creates a selection box by click and dragging nodes that
are only partially in the box are still selected.

props.name: panActivationKeyCode
props.doc:
If a key is set, you can pan the viewport while that key is held down even if `panOnScroll`
is set to `false`.

By setting this prop to `null` you can disable this functionality.

props.name: multiSelectionKeyCode
props.doc: Pressing down this key you can select multiple elements by clicking.

props.name: zoomActivationKeyCode
props.doc:
If a key is set, you can zoom the viewport while that key is held down even if `panOnScroll`
is set to `false`.

By setting this prop to `null` you can disable this functionality.

props.name: snapToGrid
props.doc: When enabled, nodes will snap to the grid when dragged.

props.name: snapGrid
props.doc: If `snapToGrid` is enabled, this prop configures the grid that nodes will snap to.

props.name: onlyRenderVisibleElements
props.doc:
You can enable this optimisation to instruct React Flow to only render nodes and edges that would be visible in the viewport.

This might improve performance when you have a large number of nodes and edges but also adds an overhead.

props.name: nodesDraggable
props.doc:
Controls whether all nodes should be draggable or not. Individual nodes can override this
setting by setting their `draggable` prop. If you want to use the mouse handlers on
non-draggable nodes, you need to add the `"nopan"` class to those nodes.

props.name: autoPanOnNodeFocus
props.doc: When `true`, the viewport will pan when a node is focused.

props.name: nodesConnectable
props.doc:
Controls whether all nodes should be connectable or not. Individual nodes can override this
setting by setting their `connectable` prop.

props.name: nodesFocusable
props.doc:
When `true`, focus between nodes can be cycled with the `Tab` key and selected with the `Enter`
key. This option can be overridden by individual nodes by setting their `focusable` prop.

props.name: nodeOrigin
props.doc:
The origin of the node to use when placing it in the flow or looking up its `x` and `y`
position. An origin of `[0, 0]` means that a node's top left corner will be placed at the `x`
and `y` position.

props.name: edgesFocusable
props.doc:
When `true`, focus between edges can be cycled with the `Tab` key and selected with the `Enter`
key. This option can be overridden by individual edges by setting their `focusable` prop.

props.name: edgesReconnectable
props.doc:
Whether edges can be updated once they are created. When both this prop is `true` and an
`onReconnect` handler is provided, the user can drag an existing edge to a new source or
target. Individual edges can override this value with their reconnectable property.

props.name: elementsSelectable
props.doc:
When `true`, elements (nodes and edges) can be selected by clicking on them. This option can be
overridden by individual elements by setting their `selectable` prop.

props.name: selectNodesOnDrag
props.doc: If `true`, nodes get selected on drag.

props.name: panOnDrag
props.doc:
Enabling this prop allows users to pan the viewport by clicking and dragging.
You can also set this prop to an array of numbers to limit which mouse buttons can activate panning.
Mouse button arrays do not disable touch panning; set this prop to `false` to disable all drag panning.

props.name: minZoom
props.doc: Minimum zoom level.

props.name: maxZoom
props.doc: Maximum zoom level.

props.name: viewport
props.doc:
When you pass a `viewport` prop, it's controlled, and you also need to pass `onViewportChange`
to handle internal changes.

props.name: defaultViewport
props.doc:
Sets the initial position and zoom of the viewport. If a default viewport is provided but
`fitView` is enabled, the default viewport will be ignored.

props.name: onViewportChange
props.doc: Used when working with a controlled viewport for updating the user viewport state.

props.name: translateExtent
props.doc:
By default, the viewport extends infinitely. You can use this prop to set a boundary.
The first pair of coordinates is the top left boundary and the second pair is the bottom right.

props.name: preventScrolling
props.doc: Disabling this prop will allow the user to scroll the page even when their pointer is over the flow.

props.name: nodeExtent
props.doc:
By default, nodes can be placed on an infinite flow. You can use this prop to set a boundary.
The first pair of coordinates is the top left boundary and the second pair is the bottom right.

props.name: defaultMarkerColor
props.doc:
Color of edge markers.
You can pass `null` to use the CSS variable `--xy-edge-stroke` for the marker color.

props.name: zoomOnScroll
props.doc: Controls if the viewport should zoom by scrolling inside the container.

props.name: zoomOnPinch
props.doc: Controls if the viewport should zoom by pinching on a touch screen.

props.name: panOnScroll
props.doc:
Controls if the viewport should pan by scrolling inside the container.
Can be limited to a specific direction with `panOnScrollMode`.

props.name: panOnScrollSpeed
props.doc:
Controls how fast viewport should be panned on scroll.
Use together with `panOnScroll` prop.

props.name: panOnScrollMode
props.doc:
This prop is used to limit the direction of panning when `panOnScroll` is enabled.
The `"free"` option allows panning in any direction.

props.name: zoomOnDoubleClick
props.doc: Controls if the viewport should zoom by double-clicking somewhere on the flow.

props.name: reconnectRadius
props.doc: The radius around an edge connection that can trigger an edge reconnection.

props.name: noDragClassName
props.doc:
If a node is draggable, clicking and dragging that node will move it around the canvas. Adding
the `"nodrag"` class prevents this behavior and this prop allows you to change the name of that
class.

props.name: noWheelClassName
props.doc:
Typically, scrolling the mouse wheel when the mouse is over the canvas will zoom the viewport.
Adding the `"nowheel"` class to an element in the canvas will prevent this behavior and this prop
allows you to change the name of that class.

props.name: noPanClassName
props.doc:
If an element in the canvas does not stop mouse events from propagating, clicking and dragging
that element will pan the viewport. Adding the `"nopan"` class prevents this behavior and this
prop allows you to change the name of that class.

props.name: fitView
props.doc: When `true`, the flow will be zoomed and panned to fit all the nodes initially provided.

props.name: fitViewOptions
props.doc:
When you typically call `fitView` on a `ReactFlowInstance`, you can provide an object of
options to customize its behavior. This prop lets you do the same for the initial `fitView`
call.

props.name: connectOnClick
props.doc:
The `connectOnClick` option lets you click or tap on a source handle to start a connection
and then click on a target handle to complete the connection.

If you set this option to `false`, users will need to drag the connection line to the target
handle to create a connection.

props.name: attributionPosition
props.doc:
By default, React Flow will render a small attribution in the bottom right corner of the flow.

You can use this prop to change its position in case you want to place something else there.

props.name: proOptions
props.doc:
By default, we render a small attribution in the corner of your flows that links back to the project.

Please only remove the attribution if you have a React Flow subscription.
More information in the {@link https://reactflow.dev/remove-attribution removing attribution guide}.

props.name: autoPanOnNodeDrag

viewport while dragging a node.

props.name: autoPanOnConnect

props.name: autoPanOnSelection

props.name: autoPanSpeed
props.doc: The speed at which the viewport pans while dragging a node or a selection box.

props.name: connectionRadius
props.doc: The radius around a handle where you drop a connection line to create a new edge.

props.name: onError
props.doc:
Occasionally something may happen that causes React Flow to throw an error.

Instead of exploding your application, we log a message to the console and then call this event handler.
You might use it for additional logging or to show a message to the user.

props.name: isValidConnection
props.doc:
This callback can be used to validate a new connection

If you return `false`, the edge will not be added to your flow.
If you have custom connection logic its preferred to use this callback over the
`isValidConnection` prop on the handle component for performance reasons.

props.name: nodeDragThreshold
props.doc:
With a threshold greater than zero you can delay node drag events.
If threshold equals 1, you need to drag the node 1 pixel before a drag event is fired.
1 is the default value, so that clicks don't trigger drag events.

props.name: connectionDragThreshold
props.doc:
The threshold in pixels that the mouse must move before a connection line starts to drag.
This is useful to prevent accidental connections when clicking on a handle.
